ownerThemes.theme: Owners single out the 16 sensor buttonholes as consistent and reliable, and describe the machine as very quiet.
A four-year owner still rates stitch quality as excellent; others report thick layers feeding well on the box feed.

QuiltingBoard members ask whether the F300 is enough machine for quilting or whether to stretch to the F600.

editorial.verdict: The HZL-F300 is the F600's chassis with 106 stitches and a smaller box, keeping the 900 spm box feed, 16 sensor buttonholes, knee lifter and auto trimmer at a lower price.
editorial.whoFor: A sewer stepping up from a beginner machine who wants Juki's box feed and buttonholes and does not need 225 stitches or the bundled walking foot and table.
editorial.skipIf: You already know you want the walking foot, wide table and hard case, in which case the F600 bundle is usually the cheaper way to get them, or you need more than 8 in of arm.
editorial.keySpec: 106 stitches · 900 spm · 8 in throat · box feed · 21.6 lb
strengths: Same box feed, 7 mm stitch width, 900 spm and 130/705H needle system as the F600.
16 sensor buttonholes that owners consistently rate as the machine's best feature.
Knee lifter and automatic thread trimmer, rare at this price.
weaknesses: Accessory set is thin; the walking foot and wide table that ship with the F600 are extras here unless bundled.
8 in arm and 900 spm, the same limits as the F600 for quilting.
Single LED light versus dual on the F600, per the comparison chart.

checks.title: Base machine or bonus package
checks.body: Sewing Machines Plus and Amazon sell bundles that add the table, walking foot or feet. Dealers disagree on whether a table is in the standard box. Read the contents list.

checks.title: Price gap to the F600
checks.body: At $799 versus roughly $1,399, the F600 adds 119 stitches, a font, a second LED and about $200 of accessories. If you need the accessories, the gap narrows fast.

checks.title: Ignore the 9 in throat claim
checks.body: An Amazon title says 9 in. Dealer spec sheets say 8 in to the right of the needle and 4.4 in high. Use 8 in.

realCost: Wide extension table (13 x 21.5 in) if not bundled

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Juki HZL-F300 and HZL-F600?
faqs.a: Both use the same 900 spm box-feed chassis with 16 buttonholes. The F300 has 106 stitches and 3 fonts, one LED and a push-button interface; the F600 has 225 stitches, 4 fonts, dual LEDs, a dial and a larger accessory set.

faqs.q: How big is the throat on the HZL-F300?
faqs.a: 8 in to the right of the needle and about 4.4 in high per dealer spec sheets. An Amazon title claiming 9 in is not supported.

faqs.q: Does the HZL-F300 come with an extension table?
faqs.a: Dealers disagree. One lists a table and knee lifter in the box; a comparison chart says no table. Bundles add a 13 x 21.5 in wide table. Check the listing.

faqs.q: Is the HZL-F300 good for quilting?
faqs.a: For piecing and small to medium quilts, owners say yes, helped by the knee lifter and drop feed. The 8 in arm limits large tops.

faqs.q: Does the HZL-F300 have an automatic thread cutter?
faqs.a: Yes, by button or by the heel of the foot controller, and an automatic needle threader.

faqs.q: What needles does the HZL-F300 use?

faqs.a: 21.6 lb on one dealer sheet, 21 lb on another.

faqs.q: What is the warranty on the HZL-F300?
faqs.a: Juki America's household warranty: 5 years materials and workmanship, 2 years on motors and electrical parts, original purchaser only. One dealer adds 90 days on adjustments.
